scene: Inferno XXX — impersonation, counterfeit florins and disputed testimony
story: Dante and Virgil continue through the tenth bolgia of falsifiers, where Gianni Schicchi and Myrrha are described as impersonators afflicted with madness and frenzy.

Gianni Schicchi assumed the identity of Buoso Donati to alter a will, while Myrrha disguised herself to deceive her father. Their impersonations concern social identities, not bodily metamorphoses like those of Canto XXV.
Master Adam, punished for counterfeiting Florentine florins, lies swollen and tormented by thirst. He remembers the clear streams of Casentino but cannot drink.
The Greek Sinon, notorious in the Trojan Horse deception, and Potiphar's wife are represented among falsifiers of testimony.
Master Adam and Sinon quarrel, accusing and striking one another; Dante lingers to hear the dispute.
Virgil sharply rebukes Dante for taking pleasure in the quarrel; Dante feels shame, and Virgil accepts his repentance.
The travellers continue; the descriptions of false identity, false money and false words remain distinguishable.
